record.paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
record.original_question: Let l:C->R+ be continuous, let e_j be the j-th coordinate direction in C^n, and write l_j(z) = l(z_j). Suppose that for each j = 1,...,n-1 an entire function F has bounded l_j-index in direction e_j, and that for every fixed (z1,...,z_{n-1}) the function of the remaining variable z_n has bounded l_n-index. Prove, or determine whether it is true, that F has bounded l_n-index in direction e_n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\geq 2$ and let $l:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{R}_+$ be a continuous positive function. For each $j=1,\dots,n$, define $l_j:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{R}_+$ by $l_j(z)=l(z_j)$, where $z=(z_1,\dots,z_n)\in\mathbb{C}^n$. Let $e_j$ denote the $j$-th standard coordinate direction in $\mathbb{C}^n$.

Recall that an entire function $F:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ is said to be of bounded $l_j$-index in the direction $e_j$ if there exists $N\in\mathbb{Z}_+$ such that for all $z\in\mathbb{C}^n$ and all $k\in\mathbb{Z}_+$,
$$\frac{1}{k!}\,\frac{\left|\partial^k F(z)/\partial z_j^k\right|}{l_j(z)^k} \leq \max_{0\le m\le N}\frac{1}{m!}\,\frac{\left|\partial^m F(z)/\partial z_j^m\right|}{l_j(z)^m}.$$
The smallest such $N$ is the $l_j$-index of $F$ in direction $e_j$.

For a fixed point $(z_1^0,\dots,z_{n-1}^0)\in\mathbb{C}^{n-1}$, the entire function $g(w)=F(z_1^0,\dots,z_{n-1}^0,w)$ of one variable is said to be of bounded $l$-index if there exists $N\in\mathbb{Z}_+$ (possibly depending on $(z_1^0,\dots,z_{n-1}^0)$) such that for all $w\in\mathbb{C}$ and all $k\in\mathbb{Z}_+$,
$$\frac{|g^{(k)}(w)|}{k!\,l(w)^k}\leq \max_{0\le m\le N}\frac{|g^{(m)}(w)|}{m!\,l(w)^m}.$$

Suppose an entire function $F:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For each $j=1,\dots,n-1$, $F$ has bounded $l_j$-index in the direction $e_j$.
\item For every fixed $(z_1^0,\dots,z_{n-1}^0)\in\mathbb{C}^{n-1}$, the entire function $w\mapsto F(z_1^0,\dots,z_{n-1}^0,w)$ has bounded $l$-index in $\mathbb{C}$.
\end{enumerate}
Determine whether $F$ must have bounded $l_n$-index in the direction $e_n$ (in the uniform sense, i.e., with a single bound $N$ valid at all points of $\mathbb{C}^n$).
artifact.status_search_result: Literature on bounded L-index in direction discusses related implications between coordinatewise and joint-variable boundedness (and a known negative answer to the Bordulyak–Sheremeta question on the converse direction), but no source located resolves this particular coordinatewise-to-direction implication conjecture. Its current status appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Analytic functions in the unit ball of bounded L-index in joint variables and of bounded L-index in direction
status_evidence.snippet: A connection between bounded L-index in joint variables and bounded L-index in direction is established.
status_evidence.claim: Related implications between coordinatewise/joint and directional bounded index are studied but the specific conjecture is not resolved in the located literature.

status_evidence.title: Slice Holomorphic Functions in Several Variables with Bounded L-Index in Direction
status_evidence.snippet: Sufficient and necessary conditions providing boundedness of L-index in the direction.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on criteria for bounded L-index in direction continues; the precise coordinatewise conjecture is not stated as solved.
